changes.text: RoboARC 1.0.1, texts and the monitor's image reference only: the texts, comments and docstrings of this task cite this repository's paths (docs/PROTOCOL.md, docs/STANDARD_MODE.md, docs/TAXONOMY.md, tools/release/release_rebuild.py, images/roboarc/) and carry no internal notes, `[task].name` is `roboarc/<dir>` (it was `robot-coding-bench/<dir>`), and the Release line names the task set's version (the image stays `ghcr.io/embodied-first-exam/roboarc:1.0.0`). The resource-monitor sidecar runs RoboARC's own build of its image, `ghcr.io/embodied-first-exam/roboarc-monitor:0.1.0` (images/monitor/; the same files and command as the earlier `ghcr.io/mll-lab-nu/efe:monitor-0.1.0`). The instruction, the logic of the grader and of the sim service, the tooling, the runtime binding, the frozen instance and the reference are unchanged: results graded under 1.0.0 stand.

RoboARC 1.1.0, the image without Genesis: `ghcr.io/embodied-first-exam/roboarc:1.1.0` is built from the Python base image with the same operating system, the same Debian package versions and the same wheels (by sha256) as 1.0.0, without genesis-world, libuipc and the packages only they used (no task of 1.0.0 ran on them: every base is MuJoCo, every family renders with nyx_direct.py). The simulator source drops its Genesis-only modules, the tooling (v20) drops the libuipc build choice and Genesis' kernel replacements, so the runtime binding names the new simulator source, tooling and runtime. The instruction, the grader, the frozen instance and the reference are unchanged; every reference replays in the new image to the end state it reaches in 1.0.0: results graded under 1.0.x stand.

RoboARC 1.1.0, every image by digest: the Dockerfiles and compose files name the simulator image and the resource monitor's image by manifest digest, `ghcr.io/embodied-first-exam/roboarc:1.1.0@sha256:85ea9003…` (images/pins.json), so a pull gets exactly the image that was validated (until now the simulator image was named by its tag). The image, the instruction, the grader, the tooling, the frozen instance and the reference are unchanged: results graded under 1.1.0 stand.

RoboARC 1.1.0, the agent container's client packages are installed from a hashed lock: `environment/client-requirements.txt` keeps the same versions and adds the sha256 of the file pip selects for the client base, and `environment/Dockerfile` installs it with `--no-deps --require-hashes`, so a build installs exactly those files or fails. The installed packages are the same files as before.

RoboARC 1.1.1, image references moved to ghcr.io/mll-lab-nu (same images, same digests): the Dockerfiles, compose files and README name `ghcr.io/mll-lab-nu/<image>:<tag>@sha256:<digest>` with the digests of 1.1.0 (images/pins.json). The runtime binding is unchanged, and nothing else changed: results graded under 1.1.0 stand.

RoboARC 1.2.0, three scenes per base (appearance seeds): seed 0 is the released scene, unchanged; seeds 1 and 2 are the same scene and physics in other colours, materials and textures. The task allows seeds 0, 1 and 2 (`[metadata.seeds]`); the runner picks the trial's seed and the image stages that seed's frozen instance against its own runtime binding (`runtime_binding.s<S>.json`, `stage_instance.py --seed-file`). `oracle` lists seed 0 and the seeds whose Harbor oracle run passed; the reference serves every seed (re-stamped with each seed's birth where it records one). Image RoboARC 1.2.0 (the seeds' simulator source and tooling); seed 0's birth, end state and render inputs are those of 1.1.x, so results graded under 1.1.x stand.

RoboARC 1.2.1, the renderer checks the GPU before it starts: `nyx_direct.py` reads the Vulkan extensions of the task's GPU and, where `VK_KHR_ray_query` is missing (GPUs without RT cores, such as V100, A100 and H100), raises `nyx_direct.UnsupportedDevice` naming what is missing, instead of letting the native renderer crash the process. There the privileged verifier grades without its replay video (`video_rendered` 0) and the agent's camera calls raise an error it can catch; standard mode needs a GPU with RT cores. On a GPU with RT cores nothing changes. The runtime binding names the new `nyx_direct.py`; the image, the instruction, the grader, the simulator tooling, the frozen instance and the reference are unchanged: results graded under 1.2.0 stand.

RoboARC 1.3.0, the simulator source and tooling of a new experimental family (wire_splicing, not in tasks/ until the owner has reviewed it): the family's code, its two opt-in grasp options (welding a wire's links between the pads, holding between the pads) and an opt-in weld work guard, which only that family's scene profile turns on. Image RoboARC 1.3.0 (simulator source and tooling v22). This task's instance, physics, instruction, grader and reference are unchanged, and so are its birth and end states (seeds 0, 1 and 2): results graded under 1.2.x stand.

RoboARC 2.1.0, image RoboARC 2.1.0: the simulator source draws a card in the five bed-bolt scenes (visual only), fixes a crash in wire_splicing's coil count on a straight tail, and lets the blanket families' release check leave out the world-fixed arm bases (see those tasks' own entries); the buzz-wire 06, 07 and 10 texts state their own loop opening. Unless this task's own entry says otherwise, its instance, physics, instruction, grader and reference are unchanged, and so are its birth and end states (seeds 0, 1 and 2): results graded under 2.0.0 stand.

RoboARC 2.2.0, image `efe:roboarc-2.2.0`: appearance seeds v2. Seeds 1 and 2 change the room's lighting, the table top's material, the table's frame and the floor, and the task's objects' colours and finishes; they are other scenes than the seeds 1 and 2 of 1.2.0-2.1.0, so results at those seeds (and aggregates over a task's seeds) are not comparable with earlier ones. Seed 0 looks and reads as in 2.1.0 unless this task's own entry says otherwise. The physics, the graders, the births and the reference rows are unchanged at every seed: results graded under 2.1.0 stand.

RoboARC 2.2.1, the same image `efe:roboarc-2.2.0`: the standard service returns mp4 video again. Its `encode_mp4` imported imageio, which the image does not ship, so a `submit` or `get_obs` with `video="mp4"` or `"both"` (and `submit`'s default, `"mp4"`) ended the episode as an infrastructure error; it now encodes with the image's ffmpeg binary (H.264, yuv420p, faststart, as before). The time limit's text also says that the agent works alone: a reply that ends its turn or asks a question ends the session. The instance, physics, grader and reference are unchanged, and so are the birth and end states: privileged results graded under 2.2.0 stand, and so do standard ones that never asked for mp4.

battery-replacement-01-i01.design: a game controller's two AA cells swapped: slide the cover open, pry each old cell up with the pry stick, pluck it out with the fingertips, lay it on the controller's back and carry it to the recycling box held from both sides, seat two new cells held from both sides with the right polarity, latch the cover
battery-replacement-01-i01.grasp_rules: assisted grasping (contact_weld_v1): a gripper whose command moves towards closed takes hold of a graspable part (cover, new_1, new_2, old_A, old_B, stick) once both fingers touch the same part inside its grasp region, the tool frame within 6 cm of it and the penetration at most 2 mm, for 0.02 s; the part then follows the gripper rigidly. Any command that opens the gripper (by more than 0.2 % of its travel) lets it go. A hold that breaks (the fingers open more than 15 %, the part drifts 1 cm / 0.15 rad from its held pose, or the hold has to push or pull its part with more than 60 N averaged over 20 ms) is lost, and the gripper must open before it can take hold again; that force is reached when, for example, a held part is pressed hard into another object. Two grippers never hold the same part; other objects are grasped physically (friction); the grippers start empty and nearly closed: open a gripper, then close it on a part to take hold. The cells' pinch rules, stated with a pinch's central angle: the angle around the cell's axis between the two fingers' contact points, 180 degrees when they press on opposite sides of a diameter (exactly: two contacts whose connecting line lies within atan(mu) of both contact normals, force closure at friction coefficient mu; across a cell, mu 1 is 90 degrees, mu 0.268 is 150 degrees). An old cell (old_A, old_B) is taken only by a pinch of at least 90 degrees: fingertips on the top of a cell seated in its slot cannot take it, a cell levered up with the pry stick can be plucked. A hold below 150 degrees is a pluck; a cell's plucks share 60 mm of travel per episode, counted from where it leaves the compartment: once they have moved it 60 mm in all, the pluck is let go (as a lost grasp: open the gripper before taking hold again), so an old cell is carried only when held from both sides (150 degrees or more). A new cell (new_1, new_2) is taken only by a pinch of at least 150 degrees. The angle is decided when the hold is taken
battery-replacement-01-i01.grasp: assisted (contact_weld_v1 on every part; the cells by the central angle of the pinch: old cells plucked at 90 deg, carried at 150, new cells at 150; the grippers start empty)

Both fingers on the wires with every contact between the pads also holds, the same way (the red wire's two legs side by side, one pad on each; the eye's two sides with the blue wire beside them). Any command that opens the gripper (by more than 0.2 % of its travel) lets it go. A hold that breaks (the fingers open more than 15 %, a held link drifts 1 cm / 0.15 rad from its held pose, the hold has to push or pull with more than 60 N averaged over 20 ms, or a weld has fed more than 0.1 J of work into the wire) is lost, and the gripper must open before it can take hold again; that force is reached when, for example, a held wire is pulled hard against the other hand or a fixture. The jig is fixed; the grippers start empty and nearly closed: open a gripper, then close it on a wire to take hold
